sentences.text: Acanthopleurus is an extinct genus of prehistoric ray-finned fish.
It belongs to the family Xenacanthidae, which is part of the order Tetraodontiformes and class Actinopterygii.
The genus was described by Agassiz in 1844 and contains three species: A. collettei, A. serratus, and A. trispinosus.
The former species A. brevis is now classified in the separate genus Cryptobalistes.
However, the Paleobiology Database classifies Acanthopleurus in the class Chondrichthyes.
This marine fish lived in the seas over modern-day Europe during the early Oligocene epoch.
The species A. collettei and the type species A. serratus both inhabited the Oligocene of Switzerland within the Matt Formation.
Another species, A. trispinosus, lived in the Oligocene of Romania.
While Agassiz originally described the genus in 1843, modern databases place it in Chondrichthyes despite its classification in Actinopterygii.
